pathogen.value: Campylobacter jejuni (also C. coli, C. lari; in layers C. hepaticus and C. bilis cause spotty liver disease)

value: contaminated water such as puddles or unchlorinated ponds
usually no visible signs in most birds
in spotty liver disease: drop in egg production, higher deaths, liver damage found at necropsy

mortality.value: usually low in poultry, but spotty liver disease outbreaks in layers can approach 15% mortality

diagnosis.value: bacterial culture of feces or liver, or PCR testing; there is no reliable blood/antibody test in birds

value: keeping birds away from muddy puddles or untreated water sources
controlling rodents, wild birds and insects

treatment_overview.value: most poultry infections need no treatment since birds show no illness; spotty liver disease outbreaks in layers may be treated with antibiotics under veterinary guidance

when_to_call_vet.value: Call a vet if egg production suddenly drops along with unexplained deaths in the flock, which can point to spotty liver disease.

summary.value: Campylobacter bacteria commonly live in the gut of healthy chickens without making them sick, but people can catch a diarrheal illness from handling backyard poultry or eating undercooked chicken. In layer flocks, certain related bacteria can occasionally cause a liver disease that drops egg production and raises deaths, but the germ itself rarely makes chickens visibly ill.
